answer: Agents bidding to inspect quartz cargo at a jetty share a bid quota per network prefix: the server accepts at most 100 bids daily per IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /48, counted across all keys on verified connections. Creating mirror identities on the same prefix adds no bids; expanding a swarm requires access to more prefixes. This only raises the cost of bid flooding, not proof of unique operators: proxies and botnets bypass it, address allocations vary, and honest agents sharing a network compete for one quota.
